title: Efficient Fault-Tolerant Single Qubit Gate Approximation And Universal Quantum Computation Without Using The Solovay-Kit

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that "universal quantum computation can be carried out using the Clifford gates Z, S, CNOT plus the non-Clifford T gate" and that "single-qubit Z, S and T gates together with two-qubit CNOT gate are sufficient to approximate any unitary operator in U(2) to arbitrary precision [1–4]". This is false: Z, S and T are all diagonal, and together with CNOT they generate only a (non-dense) subgroup; the Hadamard gate (or some non-diagonal gate) is essential. The standard universal set cited in Refs. [1-4] is {H, S, T, CNOT}. The paper itself later lists H among the FT gates and includes H in its final gate set, so the premise as stated is simply wrong.

The construction demands only Hv = w over ℝ, i.e. real-linear conditions on the *generator rows* of C. But the phase acquired by a basis state |ℓ ⊕ a⟩ under ⊗_j P(α v_j) is exp(iα Σ_j v_j (ℓ⊕a)_j), and the map x ↦ Σ_j v_j x_j is NOT F_2-linear, so satisfying the condition on the generators does not make the phase constant over the whole coset. Explicit counterexample with the paper's own Eqs. (5) and (6): v = (−1,1,0,0,0,0,1) and the codeword obtained from ℓ=0, a=1, b=0, c=1 is (0,1,0,1,1,0,1), for which v·x = 2, giving phase e^{2iα}, whereas the a=b=c=0 term gets phase 1. Hence ⊗_j P(αv_j) is not a logical phase gate and Eq. (6) is incorrect.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section, text following Eq. (4) ("the P(α)_L gate execution in Eq. (4) is transversal")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Claiming a transversal (hence fault-tolerant) implementation of P(α)_L for a continuum of angles α on a nontrivial error-correcting code contradicts the Eastin–Knill theorem, which forbids a continuous group of transversal logical gates on any error-detecting code. For the Steane code in particular it is well known that no transversal T (let alone transversal arbitrary P(α)) exists.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section (Eq. (4) vs. the recursion P(πℓ/2^m) ⇐ P(πℓ/2^{m−1}) ⇐ ···)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper's logic is internally inconsistent: if Eq. (4) really provides a transversal (and therefore FT) implementation of P(α)_L for arbitrary α, then the whole recursion plus gate-teleportation machinery, and indeed the entire approximation problem, is unnecessary — one could apply P(α)_L directly and exactly. Conversely, if only dyadic angles are obtainable through the recursion, then Eq. (4) cannot hold for arbitrary α.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions ("using O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···) gates") vs. Abstract
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims O(log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] log log log[1/ϵ]···) gates, while the conclusion states O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···) with a spurious factor of ϵ. The extra ϵ makes the expression tend to zero as ϵ→0, which is nonsensical for a gate count and contradicts the abstract.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions ("angle of rotation accurate to ϵ log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ) ···")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Two sentences earlier the required angular accuracy is δ ≤ ϵ/⌈log_2(1/ϵ)⌉, i.e. ϵ DIVIDED by the log factors. The conclusion multiplies by the log factors, which gives a *looser* tolerance than ϵ itself and would not deliver the claimed overall accuracy ϵ. The two statements contradict each other and the second is wrong in direction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions (definition of m in the gate set {H, P(πℓ/2^m)})
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper writes "m = ⌈ϵ/[log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···]⌉". Since ϵ ∈ (0,1], this expression is ≤ 1 (and tends to 0 as ϵ→0), whereas m must be of order log_2(1/δ) ≈ log_2(1/ϵ) + log_2log_2(1/ϵ) for the dyadic angle πℓ/2^m to approximate α within δ. The formula is dimensionally/asymptotically inverted.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Conclusions (gate set depending on ϵ)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Nielsen–Chuang challenge is to approximate single-qubit gates with O(log[1/ϵ]) gates drawn from a FIXED finite set, independent of ϵ. Here the gate set {H, P(πℓ/2^m)} grows with ϵ (the paper admits "a huge gate set, whose size increases as ϵ decreases, is needed"). With an ϵ-dependent set that already contains P(πℓ/2^m) for all ℓ < 2^m, a single gate suffices to approximate any phase gate, so the claimed scaling is vacuous and the stated 'partial answer' to the challenge is not an answer to the posed problem.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ("Kuperberg implies that to approximate any single-qubit gate to an accuracy of ϵ > 0 requires O(log^c[1/ϵ]) quantum gates with c > 1.44042")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Kuperberg's result is an UPPER bound (a construction achieving O(log^c[1/ϵ]) with c ≈ 1.44042 + δ, as correctly stated later in the Introduction), not a statement that this many gates are 'required'. Stating a requirement (lower bound) with big-O notation is logically incoherent and misrepresents Ref. [7]; the only known lower bound is Ω(log[1/ϵ]).

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ("a challenge to efficiently approximate single-qubit gate ... using Ω(log[1/ϵ]) gates")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Using Ω(log[1/ϵ]) gates is trivially satisfied by any construction (it is the known lower bound); the challenge is to achieve O(log[1/ϵ]) (equivalently Θ(log[1/ϵ])) gates. The asymptotic notation is used backwards, misstating the problem taken from Ref. [3].

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract / Conclusions (claimed complexity O(log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] log log log[1/ϵ]···)) versus the derivation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper's own analysis gives a recursion depth m ≈ log_2(1/δ) with δ ≈ ϵ/[log_2(1/ϵ)···], i.e. m ≈ log_2(1/ϵ) + log_2log_2(1/ϵ) + ···, which is a SUM of logarithms and therefore O(log[1/ϵ]). The headline result is instead stated as a PRODUCT of iterated logarithms, which is not what the stated procedure yields and is never derived anywhere in the paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section ("I can implement any P(πℓ/2^m) gate in a FT manner ... in O(n) times through the recursion")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The number of recursion steps in P(πℓ/2^m) ⇐ P(πℓ/2^{m−1}) ⇐ ··· ⇐ P(πℓ/4) is m−2 = O(m), i.e. O(log[1/ϵ]); it has nothing to do with n, which is defined earlier as the block length of the Steane-like code. The stated O(n) count is inconsistent with the construction and with the complexity claimed elsewhere in the paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction ("Using Steane-like code, the logical Z, H, X, S and CNOT are automatically FT")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For CSS codes built from a self-orthogonal classical code, transversal X, Z, H and CNOT follow, but transversal S implementing the logical S gate requires an additional condition on the code (e.g. doubly-even weights, as for Steane's code). It is not 'automatic' for all Steane-like codes, so the attribution to Refs. [3,4] overstates the general result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section ("Without lost of generality, I write H as [L | G]")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: H is the (n−k)×n parity-check matrix of C and G is the k×n generator matrix; the notation [L | G] denotes horizontal concatenation, which is dimensionally impossible here. What is meant is a vertical stacking of logical rows L over the rows of G (possible because C ⊆ C^⊥). As written, the block decomposition is inconsistent with the stated matrix dimensions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions ("the gates needed are drawn from the set {H, P(πℓ/2^m)}") versus title/Introduction
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims universal quantum computation, and the Introduction states that CNOT plus single-qubit gates is required for universality, yet the final gate set given contains only H and phase gates, which cannot generate entangling operations. CNOT (and the measurement/Clifford corrections used in the teleportation circuit of Fig. 2) are omitted from the stated resource list.
